description.narrative: Contract related to: Advancing Human Rights in Rwanda (AHRR) - Mu butabera nshinjyabyaha mu Rwanda - The Covid-19 pandemic is having significant negative repercussions on human rights, democracy and the rule of law in many parts of the world  and on the space for civil society organisations active in the promotion of human rights and democracy. An urgent reaction is required in the third quarter of 2021 to limit the harm done and contain further entrenchment and worsening of the situation.  The overall objective of the action is the worldwide promotion and protection of: (i) human rights and fundamental freedoms; (ii) democracy; and (iii) the rule of law. The action will achieve this so by supporting and strengthening civil society organisations (CSOs), democracy activists and human-rights defenders working on critical human rights and democracy in non-EU countries. It may also cover, where relevant, the promotion of international humanitarian law. The action will mainly be implemented through competitive processes.This action will mainly be implemented by EU delegations in-country so as to: (i) better respond to the country-specific contexts; (ii) take into account the local challenges of the current COVID-19 crisis; (iii) be as close as possible to the needs of the rights holders; and (iv) promote a sense of `ownership¿ of the action among local actors. The grants will aim at implementing the priorities listed in annex III Annex of the Regulation (EU) 2021/947 in line with Human Rights and Democracy country strategies. Implementing these priorities will also contribute to the EU action plan on human rights and democracy 2020-2024. The actions financed under the country allocations will be in line with: (i) the relevant EU action plan for human rights and democracy; (ii) EU guidelines on human rights; and (iii) the respective Human Rights and Democracy country strategies. All actions will follow a human rights based approach putting people at the centre of actions and also focus on promoting gender equality.

comment.narrative: Out of 39 recommendations given 6 have been shortlisted. That is by Ministry of Justice MINIJUST Rwanda Investigation Bureau RIB and Rwanda Correctional Services RCS. The roundtable discussions have produced 39 significant recommendations. Of these six have already been acted upon by policy makers The Ministry of Justice in Rwanda has been recommended by the round table participants to implement alternatives to detention in order to address prison overcrowding. Article 3.4.7 of the new Criminal Policy specifically focuses on this issue outlining alternative options for both detention and sentencing. The Chairman of the Rwanda Bar Association a member of the stakeholder committee highlighted this matter in a widelyread local newspaper Igihe. Com. The article titled What solves is the Solution to Rwandas Overcrowded Prisons at 174 proposes that implementing alternatives to imprisonment could lead to a significant reduction in prison overpopulation estimated at 97.38. The Rwanda Correctional Services RCS received another recommendation urging them to provide more training on mental health and human rights to their staff particularly legal and psychological officers. In response to this the RCS has developed a training curriculum with eight modules. Notably Module Two addresses Physical and Mental Wellness and Module Five focuses on Human Rights and Legal Awareness. Furthermore Rwanda Bridges to Justice RBJ the National Human Rights Commission and the RCS itself collaborated to deliver a training session on mental health and human rights to 30 legal and mental health staff members representing all prisons under RCS management. Likewise we recommended that the Rwanda Investigation Bureau RIB working with law firms to provide early legal assistance. This aimed to ensure early legal representation for suspects detained by the RIB.

The article titled What solves is the Solution to Rwandas Overcrowded Prisons at 174 proposes that implementing alternatives to imprisonment could lead to a significant reduction in prison overpopulation estimated at 97.38. In response to this the RCS has developed a training curriculum with eight modules. Notably Module Two addresses Physical and Mental Wellness and Module Five focuses on Human Rights and Legal Awareness. Furthermore Rwanda Bridges to Justice RBJ the National Human Rights Commission and the RCS itself collaborated to deliver a training session on mental health and human rights to 30 legal and mental health staff members representing all prisons under RCS management. Likewise we recommended that the Rwanda Investigation Bureau RIB working with law firms to provide early legal assistance. This aimed to ensure early legal representation for suspects detained by the RIB.

title.narrative: of Social therapists recruited & trained

description.narrative: At least 300 Social therapists recruited & trained.

comment.narrative: A total of 456 social therapists 313 male and 143 female were recruited and trained. Additionally 306 inmate leaders and RCS staff 223 male and 83 female were also recruited and trained. This included 50 people 14 male and 36 female from Nyamagabe Prison 49 people 48 male and 1 female from Huye Prison 56 people 38 male and 18 female from Musanze Prison 48 people 46 male and 2 female from Rwamagana Prison 45 people 39 male and 6 female from Nyagatare Prison and 58 people 38 male and 20 female from Nyarugenge Prison. A smaller number of 150 community social therapists 90 male and 60 female were recruited and trained to provide support within the prisons. This reduction was due to some prisons such as Musanze Nyagatare and Nyamagabe not allowing community members to enter the facilities to provide psychosocial support PSS. Furthermore this was part of a strategy for sustainability to ensure the continued provision of PSS services after the project ends.
